correctness.rationale: Global tangent/seam orthogonality is exactly a·grad f=0. Homogeneity extends this from the antisphere to all positive points of the seam. After the substitutions y_i=a_i x_i on positive normal coefficients and z_j=-a_j x_j on negative ones, the seam condition fixes equal total mass while orthogonality requires equality of reciprocal sums with strictly positive coefficients. A reciprocal sum cannot be constant on a positive simplex of dimension at least one, so each sign class has one member. The remaining coefficient equation gives the claimed square-root weight ratio, and direct substitution proves the converse.

value.rationale: The primary source makes admissible hyperplanes the mechanism of its lifting theorem and highlights non-admissible splitting as an open direction. Its weighted geometric-mean family is the canonical smooth self-dual example. An exact classification of all its everywhere-orthogonal linear seams therefore gives a natural rigidity boundary for that construction: the known pairwise seams are complete, and genuinely non-admissible behavior must be sought outside this model or under weaker conditions.
